about: A candidate playbook for ab-run (deck@variant) and runner/ab.py --data: the guard arm with the hooks this deck was left without (DESIGN.md section 36). Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: Version 4 = the mirko candidate (version 3) with answer rules and rules for the cards its engine rules starved, written from the 200 tables of ab-run #29 (seed 20261290, pool bots-v2 under their playbooks; candidate 55 wins, stock pilot 47). WHAT WAS WRONG. A play or activate rule with something to do goes before every card no rule names, so under version 3 the unnamed cards were starved (cast/drawn, stock -> candidate): Amphin Mutineer 43/50 -> 23/54, Eye of Duskmantle 25/34 -> 10/31, Charnel Serenade 34/51 -> 14/48, Watcher of Hours 24/43 -> 8/38, Vizier of Many Faces 28/40 -> 12/34, Overseer of the Damned 34/42 -> 21/44, Phyrexian Metamorph 40/50 -> 24/51, Ravenous Chupacabra 43/45 -> 31/48, Deep Analysis 39/51 -> 21/45, Foreboding Steamboat 24/43 -> 14/47, Necromancy 31/49 -> 21/53, Dream Eater 32/36 -> 30/41. Black Sun's Zenith and Toxic Deluge (AI:RemoveDeck:All) were never cast by either pilot and were in hand at 29 and 32 of the candidate's 144 losses. By the logs' creature counts (zone events), on the seat's last own turn of a loss the widest opponent had a median 11 creatures to our 4, at 14 life. RULE ORDER (base rules in brackets): 1-2 Black Sun's Zenith, x max, x_min 3, when the widest opponent has six or more creatures and more power than we have and we have three or fewer (true on one of the last three own turns in 91 of 144 losses, 11 of 55 wins), or six or more and more creatures than we have and its attack could kill us next turn; above everything, since it wants all the mana. 3 mana rocks [1]. 4 Massacre Wurm once an opponent has four creatures (one-sided), above Mirko so a turn with six mana goes to the Wurm. 5 Mirko [2]. 6 engine [3]. 7 Phyrexian Arena [4]. 8 Sinister Starfish [5]. 9 Overseer of the Damned, Ravenous Chupacabra, Shriekmaw when an opponent has a creature (Forge aims the enter triggers; Overseer's optional destroy is accepted by trigger rule 5 when an opponent has a creature). 10 Amphin Mutineer when an opponent has a creature and 6+ power (it gives the exiled creature's controller a 4/3, so not on small boards). 11 Mission Briefing [6]. 12 Rise of the Dark Realms [7]. 13 the threats: base rule 8's first nine creatures with Eye of Duskmantle after Sphinx and Watcher of Hours last (hard cast; neither was named). 14 Reanimate and Animate Dead (Forge's logic picks the target, so cast only when it agrees). 15 Necromancy and Charnel Serenade from own turn 6 (neither targets as cast, so a rule casts them as they are; by turn 6 graveyards hold creatures). 16 {forge: unnamed}: Forge chooses among the rest (Phyrexian Metamorph, Vizier of Many Faces, Connive // Concoct, Foreboding Steamboat, Dream Eater, Price of Fame, Pile On, Ephara's Dispersal, Everflowing Chalice, Rogue's Passage, encore) before the cheap creatures and draw spells: clones and the split card need Forge's choice of what to copy or which half anyway. 17 base rule 8's cheap creatures (Unshakable Tail to Thoughtbound Phantasm), split off from the threats so they no longer starve the rest. 18 Disinformation Campaign [9]. 19 cheap draw [10] with Deep Analysis added (it targets a player: Forge's agreement). 20-22 [11-13]. TRIED AND DROPPED: Toxic Deluge on the same conditions as the Zenith. Its X is paid in life (PayLife<X>), which a rule cannot set: in the local tables it was cast once with X = 0, no life paid, nothing died. Left to Forge, which never casts it. NOT WRITTEN: Counterpoint, Dream Eater's flash, Final-Word Phantom's flash window (instant speed); which creature Mirko and the reanimation spells return; Foreboding Steamboat's choice of our exiled creatures. LOCAL CHECK (16 tables of bots, seeds 20263180 and 20263181, 8 each; the second on this file exactly, the first with the two Toxic Deluge rules still in): cast/drawn over the 16, Black Sun's Zenith 3/6 (each cast with the widest opponent at 9 creatures; it killed 12, 15 and 13 opposing creatures and 1 to 3 of ours, two of those games won), Massacre Wurm 3/4 (killed 7 and 16 opposing creatures), Overseer of the Damned 4/6 (its destroy accepted and aimed at an opposing creature each time), Ravenous Chupacabra 1/1, Amphin Mutineer 4/4, Eye of Duskmantle 2/5, Charnel Serenade 3/6, Watcher of Hours 1/3, Necromancy 3/5, Deep Analysis 1/1, Phyrexian Metamorph 3/6, Foreboding Steamboat 1/3, Dream Eater 3/4, Vizier of Many Faces 0/3 (Forge's choice at rule 16 declined it). The forge rule took 20 plays (trace): Metamorph, Connive, Dream Eater, Everflowing Chalice, Rogue's Passage, encore, Brainstorm, Ransom Note, Watcher's suspend. The seat won 6 of 16: too few games to mean anything. Shipped as version 4 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #38: at 200 tables of bots (seed 20261310, opponents drawn from bots-v2 under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) 70 wins against its stock pilot's 60 (+5.0 points, 95% -4 to +14, exact test 0.31) with the attack left to Forge, the better of the two attacks on these tables (the same rules won 59 with the go-wide attack). What it casts in a share of games 15 points or more below its stock pilot on the same tables, 9 cards: Foreboding Steamboat (13 of 46 games drawn against 32 of 44), Vizier of Many Faces (19 of 44 games drawn against 30 of 40), Deep Analysis (23 of 59 games drawn against 36 of 56), Notion Rain (31 of 54 games drawn against 37 of 47), Phyrexian Metamorph (30 of 51 games drawn against 36 of 46), Counterpoint (18 of 59 games drawn against 29 of 58), Everflowing Chalice (39 of 51 games drawn against 51 of 54), Charnel Serenade (25 of 54 games drawn against 39 of 61) and 1 more. It casts 11 cards that much more often (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/second-pass/revenant-recon-forgeattack-card-diff.txt). VERSION 5 (2026-11-21), the candidate `v5`: version 4 with what passed its exam, part by part. HOOKS: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). SHIPPED 2026-11-21 as version 5. Every part passed its own exam beside version 4 on the same 200 tables at the owner's table (ab-run #46 to #55, seed 20261390; demo-data/ab/2026-11-21-ab-v25/, DESIGN.md section 35): wins of 200 where version 4 won 55: leader 56, block 58, swing 54. No two parts were played together; the version is at the tables beside version 4 in ab-run #57 (seed 20261410). VERSION 6 CANDIDATE `guard` (2026-11-21). Version 5 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared and the hooks the version already has have acted, attackers are taken back when the attack leaves the seat where the opponents one after another are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that, or, when nothing kept home does, where one opponent alone is (`"guard": "table"`; a sure kill's attackers stay, and an attack stands when nothing kept home would save the seat). No cast or trigger rule is changed. VERSION 7 CANDIDATE `full` (2026-11-22). Version 6 (the guard arm of ab-run #57, which held by its rule and ships as version 6) with what this deck was left without on 2026-11-21: free damage: creatures Forge kept home attack an opponent who cannot block (`"open": true` on the attack); its removal triggers aimed at the most dangerous opponent (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`). WHY: it was left out by a rule ("behind by more than two tables of 200") that DESIGN.md section 35 found to be close to a coin for a part worth nothing: `open` by itself beside the version before in ab-run #49 (52 against 55, 10 tables against 13, exact test 0.68); `aim` by itself beside the version before in ab-run #47 (51 against 55, 1 table against 5, exact test 0.22); none is behind beyond noise. Since then ab-run #57 has shown the hooks acting together and the guard holding, which was written for what free damage costs; and at its table of next versions 18 of the 19 deaths by a block not made were the two decks without the block hook. No cast or trigger rule is changed. At the tables beside #57's guard arm in ab-run #60 (seed 20261410, the opponents the next versions of 2026-11-21); the rule is in CLAUDE.md, In flight.
